answer.label: Not Maya Angelou — actually Joan Walsh Anglund
answer.sourceLine: The line comes from Anglund’s 1967 poetry collection A Cup of Sun (p. 15), where it reads “A bird does not sing because he has an answer. He sings because he has a song.” The familiar “it” version was pinned on Maya Angelou around 2001 and printed on a 2015 U.S. postage stamp; Angelou never claimed authorship, and Anglund confirmed the words were hers. Per Quote Investigator.

source.excerpt: A bird does not sing because he has an answer. He sings because he has a song.
trail: Poet Joan Walsh Anglund wrote “A bird does not sing because he has an answer. He sings because he has a song” in A Cup of Sun (1967), p. 15, per Quote Investigator.

The attribution drifted over decades — labeled a “Chinese proverb” by the mid-1980s, credited to others in the 1990s, and reassigned to Maya Angelou (with “it” for “he”) by around 2001, per Quote Investigator.
Wikiquote lists the line under Misattributed, calling it “a variant quote from the work of poet Joan Walsh Anglund.”
The 2015 U.S. Postal Service Maya Angelou “forever” stamp carried the misattributed wording, prompting Anglund and others to note the error, per Professor Buzzkill.
source.excerptNote: Anglund’s original uses “he.” The version credited to Maya Angelou — and printed on her 2015 stamp — swaps in “it” and compresses the two sentences into one.
source.rightsHolder: Estate of Joan Walsh Anglund / Houghton Mifflin Harcourt
source.rightsNote: The line first appeared in Joan Walsh Anglund’s A Cup of Sun (Harcourt, Brace & World, 1967). As a work first published in 1967 by an identifiable author and publisher, it is in copyright in the United States; rights rest with Anglund’s estate and her publisher.

author.name: Joan Walsh Anglund
author.heading: Joan Walsh Anglund
author.bio: Joan Walsh Anglund was a hugely popular American author and illustrator of children’s books, known for her round-faced little characters with dots for eyes and no mouths. Her debut, A Friend Is Someone Who Likes You (1958), sold millions, and she published dozens of gift books and poetry collections. The bird line appears in her 1967 verse collection A Cup of Sun.

misattribution.heading: How Maya Angelou got the credit
misattribution.intro: This is one of the most famous misattributions in American letters — so entrenched that the federal government printed it on a stamp. The words are not Maya Angelou’s.

items.why: Angelou never wrote or claimed this line. It was reassigned to her by around 2001 — likely helped by the echo of her memoir title I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings — and the U.S. Postal Service put it on her 2015 commemorative stamp. Wikiquote files it under “Misattributed.”

items.who: a “Chinese proverb,” Howard Clemmons, Lou Holtz
items.why: Before landing on Angelou, the line was labeled a “Chinese proverb” (mid-1980s and again in 1990s digests) and credited to assorted individuals, per Quote Investigator.

misattribution.truthLine: The real author is poet Joan Walsh Anglund, who wrote “A bird does not sing because he has an answer. He sings because he has a song” in A Cup of Sun (1967), p. 15 — the popular “it” wording is a later alteration, per Quote Investigator.

context.heading: The stamp that got it wrong
lead: In April 2015 the U.S. Postal Service unveiled a “forever” stamp honoring Maya Angelou, its portrait paired with the line “A bird doesn’t sing because it has an answer, it sings because it has a song.” Within days, reporters and Joan Walsh Anglund’s family pointed out that the words came from Anglund’s 1967 book A Cup of Sun, not from Angelou.

The Postal Service noted Angelou had used the line in interviews — but she had never claimed to have written it. The episode became a textbook case of how a warm, quotable sentence attaches itself to a more famous name.
context.pull: Anglund wrote “he.” The stamp said “it,” and said “Angelou.”
